title: List GitHub issues with AI by label, owner or milestone
h1: get a github issue list with the filters you mean
description: Filter a GitHub repository's issues by labels, assignee, milestone or update time. Have a bot separate pull requests and report without editing the queue.
answer: **walk into the handover knowing which issues still need an owner.** give the bot a github repository and narrow it by label, assignee, milestone or recent updates. it brings the matching work here without editing the queue. github includes pull requests too, so ask for those in a separate list.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

og_line: the queue, narrowed to your question.
what:
**get the queue down to the work you can act on.** name the assignee, label, milestone or state you need. the bot can find a milestone's number from its name.

'updated since monday' includes older issues with new activity. use opening dates when you want new issues. long lists arrive in batches of up to 100; have the bot reach the end before counting.
uses: find unassigned accessibility reports before deciding who can help
list a teammate’s issues before a coverage handover
collect a milestone’s work without moving or reprioritising it
find closed issues that picked up fresh activity this week

routine.message: every wednesday at 11, list open, unassigned issues labelled accessibility in hazelpoint/atlas-desk. finish every result batch. keep pull requests separate. show issue numbers, titles and the filters you used here. report any batch you could not read. if no issues match, say so. never assign people, add labels or close anything.
routine.needs: github connected; read only repository access
routine.output:
hazelpoint/atlas-desk
filters: open, unassigned, accessibility
#118 keyboard focus missing on search
#126 chart labels need text alternatives
pull requests excluded from the issue count.

steps: connect github with **read only** for a report that changes nothing
paste the repo link and name the label, person or milestone
read the filters beside the first result and find the separate pull request list
schedule the report, then pause it when the staffing question ends
watch: **pull requests can inflate the count.** ask for separate lists.
**old work can come back to life.** use updated for recent activity, opened for newly filed issues.
**repo names can repeat.** paste the full github link.

faq.q: can it show only issues nobody owns?
faq.a: **yes, unassigned is a supported filter.** add a label or milestone to keep the list short.

faq.q: why are old issues appearing in my weekly list?
faq.a: **someone touched them this week.** the update filter includes old issues with new activity during your chosen week.

steps: ask for open issues with one exact label
read the filters beside the issue count

mistakes.mistake: counting pull requests as unresolved reports
mistakes.fix: ask for issues and pull requests in separate groups.

mistakes.mistake: asking for new issues with an update filter
mistakes.fix: say whether you mean opening dates or recent activity.

tip.text: a count without its filters is a number you cannot plan around.
